        \qquad
        0\le i\le m,
        \quad
        0\le j\le r,$$ are $k_\mu$-linearly independent on every
connected component $C_\mu$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* By Lemma [5](#lem:component-constants){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:component-constants"}, every connected component $C_\mu$
is integral and positive-dimensional, and the field $k_\mu$ is finite.
Fix a component $C=C_\mu$ and write $k_C=k_\mu$. The set
$k_C^{(m+1)(r+1)}$ is finite. For every nonzero matrix
$$\gamma=(\gamma_{ij})\in k_C^{(m+1)(r+1)}\setminus\left\{0\right\},$$
define actual sections on the $k_C$-scheme $C$ by
$$f_i^\gamma=\sum_{j=0}^{r}\gamma_{ij}e_j|_C
        \in H^0(C,\mathcal E|_C)
        \qquad(0\le i\le m),$$ where $H^0(C,\mathcal E|_C)$ is viewed as
a $k_C$-vector space. Since the sections $e_j|_C$ are $k_C$-linearly
independent, not all $f_i^\gamma$ are zero. Let
$$V_\gamma=\bigcap_{\{i\mid f_i^\gamma\ne0\}}V_C(f_i^\gamma).$$ This is
a proper closed subset of the integral scheme $C$. Hence
$$U_\gamma=C\setminus V_\gamma$$ is a nonempty open subscheme of the
positive-dimensional integral scheme $C$, and is again finite type with
a positive-dimensional irreducible component. Apply
Lemma [4](#lem:closedpoints){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:closedpoints"} to $U_\gamma$ and to the finite set
consisting of $S\cap |U_\gamma|$ together with all previously chosen
points in $U_\gamma$. This gives a closed point
$$Q_{C,\gamma}\in U_\gamma\setminus S$$ outside all previously chosen
points. By construction,
$$(f_0^\gamma(Q_{C,\gamma}),\ldots,f_m^\gamma(Q_{C,\gamma}))
        \ne0.$$ Choose a standard basis vector
$$\epsilon^{C,\gamma}\in\left\{0,1\right\}^{m+1}\setminus\{0\}$$
corresponding to a nonzero coordinate of this vector, and prescribe
$$\epsilon_{Q_{C,\gamma},i}=\epsilon_i^{C,\gamma}.$$ Let $\mathcal R$ be
the union of all points $Q_{C,\gamma}$ over all connected components and
all nonzero matrices $\gamma$. This set is finite, because there are
finitely many connected components and finitely many nonzero matrices
over each finite field $k_C$.

Now let $h_0,\ldots,h_m$ be sections of a line bundle $\mathcal M$ whose
fibres at the points of $\mathcal R$ have been trivialized and whose
prescribed values are the above binary vectors. At $Q_{C,\gamma}$ the
chosen trivialization of $\mathcal M$ identifies the value in the fibre
of $\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal E$ with
$$\left(\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}h_i e_j\right)(Q_{C,\gamma})
        =\sum_i\epsilon_i^{C,\gamma}f_i^\gamma(Q_{C,\gamma})
        \in \mathcal E|_{Q_{C,\gamma}}.$$ The right-hand side is the
previously chosen nonzero coordinate of the vector
$(f_0^\gamma(Q_{C,\gamma}),\ldots,f_m^\gamma(Q_{C,\gamma}))$. Thus no
nontrivial $k_C$-linear combination of the products $h_i e_j$ vanishes
identically on $C$. ◻
:::

## The two coordinate blocks

Fix, once and for all, a projective closure
$$j:X\hookrightarrow\overline{X},$$ a line bundle
$\overline{\mathcal E}$ on $\overline{X}$, and sections
$\overline e_0,\ldots,\overline e_r$ as in
Lemma [18](#lem:initial){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:initial"}.
Write $$\mathcal E=j^*\overline{\mathcal E},
        \qquad
        e_i=\overline e_i|_X .$$ Put $$B=(m+1)(r+1).$$ For the rest of
the proof of Theorem [1](#thm:main){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:main"}, fix $$N\ge B+m+2,
        \qquad
        A=N+1-B.$$ Then $$A\ge m+3,
        \qquad
        N+1=A+(m+1)(r+1).$$ Set $$\Lambda=(\mathbb P^N_k)^\vee(k).$$ For
each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, choose once and for all a representative
coefficient vector $$\lambda=[a:b],$$ where $$a=(a_1,\ldots,a_A)\in k^A,
        \qquad
        b=(b_{ij})_{0\le i\le m,\,0\le j\le r}
        \in k^{(m+1)(r+1)},$$ not both zero. Multiplying this
representative by a scalar only multiplies the associated section by
that scalar and does not change any hyperplane section. With this fixed
representative, let $H_\lambda$ be the hyperplane defined by
$$L_\lambda=
        \sum_{\ell=1}^{A}a_\ell X_\ell+
        \sum_{i=0}^{m}\sum_{j=0}^{r}b_{ij}Y_{ij}.$$

### Assigned points and local anti-codes

Enumerate $\Lambda=\{\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_M\}$. We choose,
recursively, pairwise distinct closed points $$P_\lambda\in X$$ and
first-order code vectors $$\xi_{\lambda1},\ldots,\xi_{\lambda A}
        \in J_\lambda:=H^0(P_\lambda^{(2)},\mathcal O_{P_\lambda^{(2)}}).$$
Suppose this has been done for $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_{\nu-1}$, and
let $E_{\nu-1}$ be the finite set of the corresponding closed point
images in $\mathbb P^{A-1}_k$. Choose $P_{\lambda_\nu}\in X$ of
sufficiently large degree, outside the previously chosen points, using
Lemma [4](#lem:closedpoints){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:closedpoints"}. Since $\kappa(P_{\lambda_\nu})/k$ is
finite separable and $X$ is smooth at $P_{\lambda_\nu}$, the quotient
$$J_{\lambda_\nu}\longrightarrow \kappa(P_{\lambda_\nu})$$ admits a
$k$-algebra section by formal etaleness of finite separable extensions.
After choosing such a section, we identify $$J_{\lambda_\nu}=K\oplus M,
        \qquad
        K=\kappa(P_{\lambda_\nu}),
        \qquad
        M=\mathfrak m_{P_{\lambda_\nu}}/\mathfrak m_{P_{\lambda_\nu}}^2,$$
with $M^2=0$ and $\dim_KM=m$. Applying
Lemma [19](#lem:localcode){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:localcode"} to the vector $a$ attached to $\lambda_\nu$,
and choosing the degree of $P_{\lambda_\nu}$ sufficiently large, we
obtain $\xi_{\lambda_\nu\ell}$ such that $$\begin{align}
        \sum_{\ell=1}^{A}a_\ell\xi_{\lambda_\nu\ell}&=0,
        \label{eq:xi-relation}\\
        P_{\lambda_\nu}^{(2)}&\longrightarrow\mathbb P^{A-1}_k,
        \quad z\longmapsto[\xi_{\lambda_\nu1}(z):\cdots:\xi_{\lambda_\nu A}(z)]
        \quad\text{is a closed immersion,}                     \label{eq:xi-immersion}
\end{align}$$ and the closed point image avoids $E_{\nu-1}$. Thus all
closed point images obtained in this way are pairwise distinct.

Put $$S=\left\{P_\lambda\mid\lambda\in\Lambda\right\},
        \qquad
        Z=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}P_\lambda^{(2)}.$$

### The shielded Segre block

Apply Lemma [21](#lem:binary){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:binary"} to the finite set $S$ and to the fixed sections
$e_j$. We obtain a finite set $$\mathcal R\subset |X|\setminus S$$ and
nonzero binary values $\epsilon_{Qi}$ for $Q\in\mathcal R$. Choose an
ample line bundle $\mathcal A$ on the fixed projective closure
$\overline{X}$. Apply Lemma [20](#lem:shield){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:shield"} to this fixed $j:X\hookrightarrow\overline{X}$,
to $\mathcal A$, and to $S$, $Z$, $\mathcal R$, and these values. We
obtain an integer $D>0$ and sections
$$\overline h_0,\ldots,\overline h_m\in H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal M}),
        \qquad
        \overline{\mathcal M}=\mathcal A^{\otimes D}.$$ Write
$$\mathcal M=j^*\overline{\mathcal M},
        \qquad
        h_i=\overline h_i|_X .$$ Then $$h_i|_Z=0,
        \qquad
        h_i(Q)=\epsilon_{Qi}\qquad(Q\in\mathcal R),
        \qquad
        \bigcap_{i=0}^{m}V_{\overline{X}}(\overline h_i)=S.$$ By
Lemma [21](#lem:binary){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:binary"},
for every connected component $C$ the sections
$$h_i e_j\in H^0(C,(\mathcal M\otimes\mathcal E)|_C)$$ are
$k_C$-linearly independent, where $k_C$ is the algebraic closure of $k$
in $k(C)$.

For $n\ge1$ set
$$\overline h_i^{(n)}=\overline h_i^n\in H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal M}^{\otimes n}),
        \qquad
        h_i^{(n)}=h_i^n\in H^0(X,\mathcal M^{\otimes n}),$$
$$\overline{\mathcal L}_n=\overline{\mathcal M}^{\otimes n}\otimes\overline{\mathcal E},
        \qquad
        \mathcal L_n=j^*\overline{\mathcal L}_n=\mathcal M^{\otimes n}\otimes\mathcal E,$$
and
$$\overline w_{ij}^{(n)}=\overline h_i^{(n)}\overline e_j\in H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal L}_n),
        \qquad
        w_{ij}^{(n)}=h_i^{(n)}e_j\in H^0(X,\mathcal L_n).$$ Since
$\epsilon^n=\epsilon$ for $\epsilon\in\left\{0,1\right\}$, the same
binary tests show that the sections $w_{ij}^{(n)}$ are $k_C$-linearly
independent on every connected component $C$ for every $n\ge1$. Moreover
$$\overline w_{ij}^{(n)}|_Z=0,
        \qquad
        \bigcap_{i,j}V_{\overline{X}}(\overline w_{ij}^{(n)})=S,$$
because the $\overline e_j$ have no common zero on $\overline{X}$ and
the $\overline h_i$ have common zero set $S$.

::: {#lem:T .lemma}
**Lemma 22** (Finite tests for componentwise nondegeneracy). *For every
connected component $C$ of $X$, let $k_C$ be the algebraic closure of
$k$ in $k(C)$. There exists a finite reduced subscheme
$$T_C\subset C\setminus S$$ such that $\mathcal R\cap C\subset T_C$,
$$\dim_{k_C} H^0(T_C,\mathcal O_{T_C})\ge N+1,$$ and, for every $n\ge1$,
the restrictions $$w_{ij}^{(n)}|_{T_C}
        \in H^0(T_C,\mathcal L_n|_{T_C})$$ are $k_C$-linearly
independent.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Fix a connected component $C$ and give
$$T_C^{(0)}:=\mathcal R\cap C$$ the reduced finite subscheme structure.
Since $\mathcal R\subset |X|\setminus S$, we have
$T_C^{(0)}\subset C\setminus S$. For every nonzero matrix
$$\gamma=(\gamma_{ij})\in k_C^{(m+1)(r+1)},$$
Lemma [21](#lem:binary){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:binary"}
gives a point $Q_{C,\gamma}\in\mathcal R\cap C=T_C^{(0)}$ such that
$$\left(\sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij}h_i e_j\right)(Q_{C,\gamma})\ne0.$$ At
every point of $\mathcal R$ the values $h_i$ are $0$ or $1$, so
$h_i(Q)^n=h_i(Q)$ for all $n\ge1$. Hence the same point detects the
corresponding linear combination of the sections
$w_{ij}^{(n)}=h_i^n e_j$ for every $n\ge1$. Therefore the restrictions
$$w_{ij}^{(n)}|_{T_C^{(0)}}$$ are $k_C$-linearly independent for every
$n\ge1$.

If $$\dim_{k_C}H^0(T_C^{(0)},\mathcal O_{T_C^{(0)}})\ge N+1,$$ set
$T_C=T_C^{(0)}$. Otherwise, add closed points of
$C\setminus(S\cup\mathcal R)$, each time avoiding the finite set already
chosen and using Lemma [4](#lem:closedpoints){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:closedpoints"} over the finite field $k_C$, until the
resulting finite reduced subscheme $T_C$ satisfies
$$\dim_{k_C}H^0(T_C,\mathcal O_{T_C})
        =\sum_{P\in T_C}[\kappa(P):k_C]
        \ge N+1.$$ The inclusion $\mathcal R\cap C\subset T_C$ holds by
construction, and adding points cannot destroy the already established
linear independence. ◻
:::

Let $$T=\coprod_C T_C.$$ By
Lemma [2](#lem:interpolation-projective){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:interpolation-projective"}, after replacing $n$ by a
sufficiently large integer, the restriction map $$\begin{equation}
\label{eq:globalinterpolation}
        H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal L}_n)
        \longrightarrow
        H^0(Z,\overline{\mathcal L}_n|_Z)\oplus H^0(T,\overline{\mathcal L}_n|_T)
\end{equation}$$ is surjective. Fix such an $n$ for the remainder of the
proof and write $$\overline{\mathcal L}=\overline{\mathcal L}_n,
        \qquad
        \mathcal L=\mathcal L_n,
        \qquad
        \overline w_{ij}=\overline w_{ij}^{(n)},
        \qquad
        w_{ij}=w_{ij}^{(n)}.$$

## Prescribing the anti-code block

We now choose global sections
$$\overline u_1,\ldots,\overline u_A\in H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal L})$$
and write $u_\ell=\overline u_\ell|_X$. There are two independent
requirements. On $Z$, the first jets force the hyperplane $\lambda$ to
vanish on $P_\lambda^{(2)}$. On $T$, the values complement the shielded
block to force componentwise nondegeneracy.

### Restrictions on the assigned first-order neighbourhoods

For each $\lambda\in\Lambda$, choose a trivialization of
$\overline{\mathcal L}$ over $P_\lambda^{(2)}$ and transport the already
constructed elements $\xi_{\lambda\ell}\in J_\lambda$ to elements
$$\eta_{\lambda\ell}
        \in H^0(P_\lambda^{(2)},\overline{\mathcal L}|_{P_\lambda^{(2)}})
        \qquad(1\le\ell\le A).$$ Then
[\[eq:xi-relation\]](#eq:xi-relation){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:xi-relation"} and
[\[eq:xi-immersion\]](#eq:xi-immersion){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:xi-immersion"} become $$\begin{align}
        \sum_{\ell=1}^{A}a_\ell\eta_{\lambda\ell}&=0,                 \label{eq:anti-relation}\\
        P_\lambda^{(2)}&\longrightarrow\mathbb P^{A-1}_k,
        \quad z\longmapsto [\eta_{\lambda1}(z):\cdots:\eta_{\lambda A}(z)]
        \quad\text{is a closed immersion.}                       \label{eq:anti-local-immersion}
\end{align}$$ Because the closed point images for different $\lambda$
are pairwise distinct, the scheme-theoretic images of the summands
$P_\lambda^{(2)}$ have pairwise disjoint supports in
$\mathbb P^{A-1}_k$.
Lemma [14](#lem:finite-disjoint-closed-immersion){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:finite-disjoint-closed-immersion"} therefore shows that
the disjoint union map $$Z=\coprod_{\lambda\in\Lambda}P_\lambda^{(2)}
        \longrightarrow\mathbb P^{A-1}_k$$ defined by the
$\eta_{\lambda\ell}$ is a closed immersion.

Equivalently, for $1\le\ell\le A$ we have prescribed a section
$$\eta_\ell=(\eta_{\lambda\ell})_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
        \in H^0(Z,\overline{\mathcal L}|_Z)$$ with the property that, on
the summand $P_\lambda^{(2)}$, $$\begin{equation}
\label{eq:anti-Z-global}
        \sum_{\ell=1}^{A}a_\ell\eta_\ell=0.
\end{equation}$$

### Restrictions on the component tests

For a connected component $C$, let $k_C$ be the algebraic closure of $k$
in $k(C)$ and set $$V_C=H^0(T_C,\overline{\mathcal L}|_{T_C}),$$ viewed
as a $k_C$-vector space. Since $T_C$ is finite and reduced and
$\overline{\mathcal L}|_{T_C}$ is invertible,
$$\dim_{k_C}V_C=\dim_{k_C}H^0(T_C,\mathcal O_{T_C}).$$ By
Lemma [22](#lem:T){reference-type="ref" reference="lem:T"}, the vectors
$$w_{ij}|_{T_C}\in V_C$$ are $k_C$-linearly independent; their span has
dimension $B$. Since $$\dim_{k_C}V_C\ge N+1=A+B,$$ we may choose vectors
$$\upsilon_{1,C},\ldots,\upsilon_{A,C}\in V_C$$ such that
$$\begin{equation}
\label{eq:component-basis}
        \upsilon_{1,C},\ldots,\upsilon_{A,C},
        \quad
        w_{00}|_{T_C},w_{01}|_{T_C},\ldots,w_{mr}|_{T_C}
\end{equation}$$ are $k_C$-linearly independent in $V_C$. Combining the
components gives $$\upsilon_\ell=(\upsilon_{\ell,C})_C
        \in H^0(T,\overline{\mathcal L}|_T)
        \qquad(1\le\ell\le A).$$

By the surjectivity of
[\[eq:globalinterpolation\]](#eq:globalinterpolation){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:globalinterpolation"}, choose global sections
$$\overline u_1,\ldots,\overline u_A\in H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal L})$$
satisfying $$\begin{align}
        \overline u_\ell|_Z&=\eta_\ell,                                  \label{eq:u-on-Z}\\
        \overline u_\ell|_T&=\upsilon_\ell.                              \label{eq:u-on-T}
\end{align}$$ Set $u_\ell=\overline u_\ell|_X$.

## The embedding and the hyperplane singularities

Consider the ordered collection of sections
$$\overline u_1,\ldots,\overline u_A,
        \overline w_{00},\ldots,\overline w_{mr}
        \in H^0(\overline{X},\overline{\mathcal L}).$$

::: {#lem:basepoint .lemma}
**Lemma 23** (No base points). *The sections
$$\overline u_1,\ldots,\overline u_A,
        \overline w_{00},\ldots,\overline w_{mr}$$ have no common zero
on $\overline{X}$. Consequently their restrictions $$u_1,\ldots,u_A,
        w_{00},\ldots,w_{mr}$$ have no common zero on $X$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* If $x\notin S$, then not all $\overline h_i(x)$ vanish and not
all $\overline e_j(x)$ vanish, so some product
$$\overline w_{ij}(x)=\overline h_i(x)^n\overline e_j(x)$$ is nonzero.
If $x=P_\lambda\in S$, then
[\[eq:anti-local-immersion\]](#eq:anti-local-immersion){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:anti-local-immersion"} implies that the anti-code values
$$\eta_{\lambda1},\ldots,\eta_{\lambda A}$$ are not all zero at
$P_\lambda$; by [\[eq:u-on-Z\]](#eq:u-on-Z){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:u-on-Z"}, the same is true for the $\overline u_\ell$. ◻
:::

By Lemma [23](#lem:basepoint){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:basepoint"}, the ordered collection defines a morphism
$$\overline\iota_N:\overline{X}\longrightarrow\mathbb P^N_k.$$ Let
$$\iota_N=\overline\iota_N|_X:X\longrightarrow\mathbb P^N_k.$$ Thus, for
$x\in X$, $$\begin{equation}
\label{eq:iota}
        \iota_N(x)=
        [u_1(x):\cdots:u_A(x):w_{00}(x):w_{01}(x):\cdots:w_{mr}(x)].
\end{equation}$$

::: {#lem:embedding .lemma}
**Lemma 24** (Local immersion and point separation). *The morphism
$\iota_N$ is a locally closed embedding.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* On $\overline{X}\setminus S$, the $\overline w$-block has no
common zero and is the Segre product of
$$\overline h^{(n)}:\overline{X}\setminus S\longrightarrow\mathbb P^m_k,
        \qquad
        x\longmapsto[\overline h_0(x)^n:\cdots:\overline h_m(x)^n]$$ and
the fixed closed immersion
$$\overline e:\overline{X}\longrightarrow\mathbb P^r_k.$$ Thus
$$\overline{X}\setminus S\longrightarrow\mathbb P^{B-1}_k,
        \qquad
        x\longmapsto[\overline w_{00}(x):\cdots:\overline w_{mr}(x)]$$
is the composition
$$\overline{X}\setminus S\xrightarrow{(\overline h^{(n)},\overline e)}\mathbb P^m_k\times\mathbb P^r_k
        \xrightarrow{\operatorname{Segre}}\mathbb P^{B-1}_k.$$ The
second projection of $(\overline h^{(n)},\overline e)$ is the locally
closed embedding $\overline e|_{\overline{X}\setminus S}$, so
$(\overline h^{(n)},\overline e)$ is a locally closed embedding; the
Segre map is a closed embedding. Hence the $\overline w$-block defines a
locally closed embedding of $\overline{X}\setminus S$.

On $Z$, all $\overline w_{ij}$ vanish and the $\overline u$-block
defines a closed immersion $Z\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^{A-1}_k$ by
construction. Since $S\subset X$ and $X$ is a smooth open subscheme of
$\overline{X}$, the set $S$ is contained in the smooth locus of
$\overline{X}$. Lemma [23](#lem:basepoint){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:basepoint"} says that the full collection of sections has
no common zero on $\overline{X}$. Therefore the hypotheses of
Lemma [16](#lem:two-block-separation){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:two-block-separation"} are satisfied for
$Y=\overline{X}$, with the $B$ sections $w_1,\ldots,w_B$ enumerated as
the $\overline w_{ij}$. Hence

::: {#lem:nondegenerate .lemma}
**Lemma 25** (Componentwise nondegeneracy). *For every connected
component $C$ of $X$, every field extension $K/k$, and every connected
component $D$ of $C_K$, the image of $D$ under $(\iota_N)_K$ is not
contained in any hyperplane of $\mathbb P^N_K$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* Let $C$ be a connected component and let $k_C$ be the algebraic
closure of $k$ in $k(C)$. Suppose that a $k_C$-linear combination
$$s=\sum_{\ell=1}^{A}\alpha_\ell u_\ell+
        \sum_{i=0}^{m}\sum_{j=0}^{r}\beta_{ij}w_{ij}
        \in H^0(C,\mathcal L|_C)$$ vanishes identically on $C$.
Restricting to $T_C$ gives
$$\sum_{\ell=1}^{A}\alpha_\ell \upsilon_{\ell,C}
        +\sum_{i,j}\beta_{ij}w_{ij}|_{T_C}=0
        \quad\text{in}\quad H^0(T_C,\mathcal L|_{T_C}),$$ where the
target is viewed as a $k_C$-vector space. By
[\[eq:u-on-T\]](#eq:u-on-T){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:u-on-T"}, $u_\ell|_{T_C}=\upsilon_{\ell,C}$ for every
$\ell$, and the construction preceding
[\[eq:component-basis\]](#eq:component-basis){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:component-basis"} chooses the vectors so that
$$\upsilon_{1,C},\ldots,\upsilon_{A,C},
        \quad
        w_{00}|_{T_C},w_{01}|_{T_C},\ldots,w_{mr}|_{T_C}$$ are
$k_C$-linearly independent in $H^0(T_C,\mathcal L|_{T_C})$. This is
exactly
[\[eq:component-basis\]](#eq:component-basis){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:component-basis"}. Hence every coefficient $\alpha_\ell$
and $\beta_{ij}$ is zero. The coordinate sections are therefore
$k_C$-linearly independent on $C$.

By Lemma [23](#lem:basepoint){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:basepoint"}, these $N+1$ coordinate sections are
basepoint-free on $C$.
Lemma [7](#lem:component-base-change){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:component-base-change"}, applied to them, gives the
asserted linear nondegeneracy on every connected component after every
scalar extension $K/k$. ◻
:::

We now prove that every rational hyperplane section is singular. Let
$$\lambda=[a:b]\in\Lambda=(\mathbb P^N_k)^\vee(k).$$ The pullback of
$H_\lambda$ is the section $$s_\lambda=
        \sum_{\ell=1}^{A}a_\ell u_\ell+
        \sum_{i=0}^{m}\sum_{j=0}^{r}b_{ij}w_{ij}
        \in H^0(X,\mathcal L).$$ At the assigned point $P_\lambda$,
every $w_{ij}$ vanishes on $P_\lambda^{(2)}$ because every $h_i$
vanishes on $Z$. By
[\[eq:anti-Z-global\]](#eq:anti-Z-global){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:anti-Z-global"} and
[\[eq:u-on-Z\]](#eq:u-on-Z){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:u-on-Z"},
$$\left.\sum_{\ell=1}^{A}a_\ell u_\ell\right|_{P_\lambda^{(2)}}=0.$$
Therefore $$\begin{equation}
\label{eq:singular-jet}
        s_\lambda|_{P_\lambda^{(2)}}=0.
\end{equation}$$ Let $C_\lambda$ be the connected component of $X$
containing $P_\lambda$. By
Lemma [25](#lem:nondegenerate){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:nondegenerate"}, the image of $C_\lambda$ is not
contained in the rational hyperplane $H_\lambda$, so
$s_\lambda|_{C_\lambda}$ is not identically zero. Since $C_\lambda$ is
integral, the germ of $s_\lambda$ at $P_\lambda$ is nonzero: if the germ
were zero, then $s_\lambda$ would vanish on a nonempty open
neighbourhood of $P_\lambda$, hence at the generic point of $C_\lambda$,
and therefore identically on $C_\lambda$.

Since $\iota_N$ is a locally closed embedding, the scheme-theoretic
intersection $H_\lambda\cap\iota_N(X)$ is identified near $P_\lambda$
with the zero scheme of $s_\lambda$ on $X$. Trivialize $\mathcal L$ near
$P_\lambda$ and let $$0\ne f_\lambda\in R:=\mathcal O_{X,P_\lambda}$$
represent $s_\lambda$. Equation
[\[eq:singular-jet\]](#eq:singular-jet){reference-type="eqref"
reference="eq:singular-jet"} says
$$f_\lambda\in\mathfrak m_{P_\lambda}^2.$$ The local ring of the
hyperplane section at $P_\lambda$ is $$R/(f_\lambda).$$ The ring $R$ is
a regular local domain of dimension $m$, because $X$ is smooth of pure
dimension $m$ over $k$.
Lemma [17](#lem:first-order-singular){reference-type="ref"
reference="lem:first-order-singular"} applies to the nonzero element
$f_\lambda\in\mathfrak m_{P_\lambda}^2$ and shows that $R/(f_\lambda)$
is not regular. Since every smooth scheme over a field is regular, the
hyperplane section is not smooth at the image point
$\iota_N(P_\lambda)$; indeed it is singular there.

This proves Theorem [1](#thm:main){reference-type="ref"
reference="thm:main"} with $$N_X=B+m+2=(m+1)(r+1)+m+2.$$

## Consequences and comparison

::: {#cor:poonen .corollary}
**Corollary 26** (Negative answer to Baker's question for a prescribed
variety). *Let $X$ be nonempty smooth quasiprojective of pure positive
dimension over $\mathbb F_q$. There is no integer $n_0$ such that every
embedding $$\iota:X\hookrightarrow\mathbb P^n_k,
        \qquad n\ge n_0,$$ satisfying Poonen's componentwise
nondegeneracy hypothesis admits a $k$-rational hyperplane
$H\subset\mathbb P^n_k$ for which $H\cap\iota(X)$ is smooth of dimension
$\dim X-1$.*
:::

::: proof
*Proof.* For every $N\ge N_X$,
Theorem [1](#thm:main){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:main"} gives
an embedding $\iota_N$ satisfying the nondegeneracy hypothesis, even
after arbitrary scalar extension, but for which every $k$-rational
hyperplane section is singular at its assigned point. ◻
:::

::: remark
Theorem [1](#thm:main){reference-type="ref" reference="thm:main"} should
be read as a construction of counterexample embeddings for the
prescribed variety $X$. It does not classify all high-dimensional
embeddings of $X$. The point is that, after $X$ is fixed, the
construction supplies embeddings satisfying Poonen's componentwise
nondegeneracy hypothesis but having no smooth $k$-rational hyperplane
section. In fact this can be done for every $N\ge N_X$.

Every rational hyperplane is assigned a specific singular point at which
the pulled-back equation has zero first jet:
$$\forall\lambda\in(\mathbb P^N_k)^\vee(k)
        \quad
        \exists P_\lambda\in X
        \quad
        s_\lambda\in\mathfrak m_{P_\lambda}^2\mathcal L_{P_\lambda}.$$
The construction does not assert that the embeddings are given by
complete linear series. This is consistent with Erman--Wood's
complete-linear-series construction for special projective examples and
with their observation that a construction for a prescribed $X$ should
not generally use complete linear series [@ErmanWood2015 Remark 9.4].
:::

::: remark
The finite-field obstruction is not merely that the dual projective
space has finitely many $k$-points. For each
$$\lambda=[a:b]\in(\mathbb P^N_k)^\vee(k)$$ one must impose the
zero-first-jet condition $$\sum_\ell a_\ell u_\ell+
        \sum_{i,j}b_{ij}h_i^n e_j
        \equiv0\pmod{\mathfrak m_{P_\lambda}^2}$$ while keeping the same
coordinate system basepoint-free, immersive at $S$, immersive away from
$S$, point-separating, and nondegenerate on each component. The shielded
block makes all $b$-terms vanish modulo $\mathfrak m_{P_\lambda}^2$ at
the assigned points, while the anti-code block absorbs the one remaining
$a$-relation without losing the first-order embedding of
$P_\lambda^{(2)}$. The auxiliary finite sets $\mathcal R$ and $T_C$
prevent these local singularity requirements from collapsing the global
image into a rational hyperplane.
:::
